/- Formalization notes:
- Since every $\|\theta n_k\|$ lies in $[0,1/2]$, the literal reading of "$\{\|\theta n_k\|\}$
  is not dense in $[0,1]$" would be vacuously true. The intended (and solved) content is that
  the sequence $(\theta n_k)$ is not dense modulo one, which is how the conclusion is rendered
  here: `¬ Dense (Set.range fun k => (↑(θ * n k) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))`. This matches
  `pollington_de_mathan` in `Problem10_6.lean` of the Bugeaud collection, which formalizes the
  full-Hausdorff-dimension version of the same de Mathan–Pollington theorem. It is implied by
  the $\inf_{k\geq 1}\|\theta n_k\| > 0$ that de Mathan and Pollington prove.
- The lacunarity hypothesis is rendered by the house predicate `IsLacunary`
  ($\exists c > 1$ with $c \cdot n_k < n_{k+1}$ for all sufficiently large $k$), as in
  `erdos_355`; for a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers the problem's condition
  $n_{k+1} \geq (1+\epsilon) n_k$ for all $k$ implies `IsLacunary`, and modifying finitely many
  terms does not affect density modulo one.
-/

/--
Let $A=\{n_1<n_2<\cdots\}\subset \mathbb{N}$ be a lacunary sequence (so there exists some
$\epsilon>0$ with $n_{k+1}\geq (1+\epsilon)n_k$ for all $k$). Must there exist an irrational
$\theta$ such that
$$\{ \|\theta n_k\| : k\geq 1\}$$
is not dense in $[0,1]$ (where $\| x\|$ is the distance to the nearest integer)?

Solved independently by de Mathan [dM80] and Pollington [Po79b], who showed that, given any
such $A$, there exists such a $\theta$, with
$$\inf_{k\geq 1}\| \theta n_k\| \gg \frac{\epsilon^4}{\log(1/\epsilon)}.$$
This bound was improved by Katznelson [Ka01], Akhunzhanov and Moshchevitin [AkMo04], and
Dubickas [Du06], before Peres and Schlag [PeSc10] improved it to
$$\inf_{k\geq 1}\| \theta n_k\| \gg \frac{\epsilon}{\log(1/\epsilon)},$$
and note that the best bound possible here would be $\gg \epsilon$.

This problem has consequences for [894](https://www.erdosproblems.com/894).

The conclusion "$\{\|\theta n_k\|\}$ is not dense in $[0,1]$" is formalized as the sequence
$(\theta n_k)$ not being dense modulo one; see the formalization notes above.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jayyhk/erdos-lean/blob/110d489ed5c07e5b216453e092e9113127c98c9a/problems/464/Erdos464.lean"]
theorem erdos_464 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ n : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono n → (∀ k, 0 < n k) → IsLacunary n →
      ∃ θ : ℝ, Irrational θ ∧
        ¬ Dense (Set.range fun k => (↑(θ * n k) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

end Erdos464

reformulations.difference: The source requires n_(k+1) ≥ (1 + ε)n_k for every index, whereas IsLacunary requires c n_k < n_(k+1) only eventually, for some c > 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under StrictMono n and positivity, these conditions are equivalent. An eventual growth constant can be reduced to accommodate the finitely many initial ratios, all of which exceed 1. More explicitly, if the eventual condition starts at N, ε = min(c − 1, 1/(n N + 1)) works: initial integer gaps are at least 1, and the eventual bound handles the tail. Conversely, an all-index bound with ε > 0 gives the strict bound with c = 1 + ε/2. Proved as Review464.lacunarity_equiv in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without sorry-dependent axioms.

reformulations.difference: The Lean conclusion uses nondensity in AddCircle (1 : ℝ), rather than nondensity of fractional parts in the unit interval as in the original papers. The website instead writes nearest-integer distances, a literal wording error explicitly addressed by the file.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every real sequence f, density of its residue classes in ℝ/ℤ is equivalent to [0,1] being contained in the closure of the fractional parts of f. The quotient map is continuous and surjective on [0,1]; conversely, its restriction to interior subintervals identifies the ordinary fractional-part representatives, so circle density forces density throughout (0,1), hence also at the endpoints. This equivalence was proved as Review464.dense_circle_iff_fractional_parts. Review464.source_statement_equiv combines it with the lacunarity equivalence to prove equivalence with the exact theorem type. The interpretation is independently supported by Erdős (1975, p. 96), Erdős–Graham (1980, p. 92), Erdős (1982, p. 63), and Pollington (1979, p. 511). It is not claimed equivalent to the website's trivially true literal nearest-integer-distance wording.

review.notes: Checked the sole declaration, including quantifier scope, positivity, irrationality, coercions, answer polarity, and boundary cases. The sequence n k = 2^k satisfies all hypotheses; constant sequences are excluded. Additional Lean checks establish invariance under deleting a finite prefix and normalization of an irrational θ to (0,1). The linked external proof was replayed after mechanical tactic-compatibility changes (convert → convert! and allowing no-progress ring_nf). /workspace/review/proof-bridge.lean proves the exact repository theorem type with axioms only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The solved category, positive answer, and formal-proof record agree with the source. Full texts of AkMo04, Ka01, and dM80 were unavailable; their contextual results were corroborated by the accessible Peres–Schlag and Dubickas papers. The audited file was not modified.
